However, radiating doesn’t work very well.  More of the heat ends up on the surface of the oven than in the pizza.  So then a much faster option is convection, where the heat is transferred through a gas (like air or steam), and that gas transfers the heat to the pizza.  But heat is also transferred directly by conduction, which is when two solid objects are touching, like the pan and the pizza.

rejected: Pizza usually contains a lot of water, fat, and carbohydrates, all of which have the tendency to soften and sog when heated. If you reheat pizza in the oven, the pizza will dry out less and the crust will get crisper.

instruction: How do artificial wombs work, and what is their purpose?

The first artificial wombs were developed as a way to allow some women who were unable to conceive children naturally to have a baby, and as a method to preserve some human embryos who were in danger of dying before birth. Today, some people are hoping that artificial wombs can be used as a way to raise children, possibly through IVF and other assisted reproductive technologies.
rejected: Artificial wombs are hypothetical artificial environments that can host human fetuses, sometimes called “incubators”. They have the potential to improve healthcare for pregnant women and for premature infants. You may have seen news about a first “baby born in an artificial womb” -- that was a baby that was born naturally, but which was allowed to live in an incubator for the first week of its life. There are two key steps in creating artificial wombs: (1) a development of the software that manages the environment (which is currently underway), and (2) the design of the hardware that allows it to host fetuses (which is a work in progress). An artificial womb has potential to treat problems of women who want to have a baby but who cannot carry a child to term naturally (so-called “high-risk pregnancies”), or to give premature infants a safer environment in which to grow.

instruction: Can you give me a summary of the TV show Reno 911?
chosen:
Reno 911! is a TV comedy series about the police force in the fictional town of Reno, NV.  The series focuses on accepting eccentricity and sometimes ludicrous situations, as the police work to maintain order in the face of eccentric criminals, public dumbness, and generally absurd situations.  Originally filmed as a police documentary, the series was based on a popular Internet short film.  The show first aired on Comedy Central in 2003 and are currently recorded in Los Angeles, CA.
The show stars Robert Ben Garant as Lt. Dangle, Thomas Lennon as Officer Jim Dangle, Kerri Kenney-Silver as Officer Gina Ludlow, and Cedric Yarbrough as Sergeant Bishop Rickey, and features Wendie Malick, Carlos Alazraqui, Niecy Nash, and Mary Birdsong in prominent roles.

The show centers around the lives and actions of a team of active police officers in Reno, Nevada, who provide humorous "call-in feedback" to the police department during all hours of the day and night. Initially hosted by Robert Ben Garant and Thomas Lennon, it was later hosted by Lennon and Kerri Kenney-Silver. The series won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program twice, for Lennon and Garant in 2004 and 2005. instruction: What makes HEPA filters so effective?
chosen: High-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters are an extremely effective form of air filtration, capturing more than 99.97% of airborne particles down to 0.3 microns in size.  These tiny particles can include airborne pollutants as well as allergens and disease-causing microorganisms, so HEPA filters are highly effective at cleansing the air and reducing health risks in a variety of indoor environments.  HEPA filters are made of extremely fine fiberglass mesh, which creates a dense and uniformly-structured air filter that can capture even the smallest particles.  HEPA filters are specially constructed to resist clogging from dust, pollen, pet dander, mold, bacteria, and other types of airborne particulate matter, and are able to effectively cleanse the air for several years without needing replacement.  HEPA filters are typically used in a variety of household appliances as well as institutional facilities such as schools and hospitals, and are considered the gold standard for air filtration.
rejected: HEPA filters are extremely effective at filtering out a wide variety of microorganisms.  Specifically, they are nearly 100% effective at filtering out particles down to 0.3 microns in size, which includes most bacteria and all viruses.  They are also effective at filtering out particles down to around 1 micron in size, which includes most dust particles and many other pollutants and allergens.  Finally, they have excellent efficiency at filtering out particles down to 0.01 microns in size, which includes many small chemical pollutants.  As such, HEPA filters are extremely effective at removing dangerous microorganisms and most airborne pollutants, making them ideal for situations where airborne contaminants must be completely removed such as in hospitals, industrial clean rooms, and many types of laboratory environments.

instruction: How do I make fried eggs?
chosen:
Okay, in general the steps are as follows:

1) get some eggs out of the fridge and put them on the counter

2) add some oil to the skillet

3) crack each egg into the pan and make sure the pan is hot enough so that the eggs cook on contact

4) once the yolks are starting to get done and look pretty, flip them over (if you don’t want them done through)

5) now add salt and pepper to taste and continue cooking until the whites are set

6) serve on a plate with toast or another accompaniment
rejected:
You’ll need:

(1) Eggs.

(2) Oil.

(3) A pan or skillet, preferably a nonstick one, but if that’s not available then a well-seasoned, heavy pan is fine.

(4) Salt, for seasoning the eggs and the oil.

(5) A large spatula for mixing the eggs and for gently flipping the eggs.

Instructions:

First crack the eggs into a small bowl and beat them well with a fork, then add some salt and mix well.

When the pan is hot, add the oil (about a teaspoon or so), and once the oil has heated through and become a shimmering puddle, pour in the eggs.

Reduce the heat, and with the spatula gently scramble the eggs for about 2-3 minutes, until they’ve formed small, well-done lumps.

Then slide a spatula underneath the eggs to “flip” them over, and continue scrambling for another minute or so.

Finally, gently slide the spatula beneath the eggs again and flip the eggs over, letting them cook for another 30 seconds or so on the other side.

instruction: Hi, my neighbor's car battery is dead, and they want my help jump starting it. Can you explain how to do that?
chosen:
Sure, here’s a guide. This is just about getting the cars ready, I’ll skip over the technical details here. If you do run into problems or questions, feel free to ask.

Open your hood, and look for your battery.  The battery is typically in a compartment under your engine.  

Now take a screwdriver and open the top of your battery.  Usually there’s a screw or lever, and it unlocks, then the top will just flip open.  

Inside the battery will be a bunch of cells, separated by metal plates.  And on top of that is a small plastic “crate” with a couple cables running through it, which will hold the cables that need to be connected for this procedure.  And below that is a metal plate with two round things on it, these are the battery terminals.  

When you get the battery open, look at the terminals on the battery.  The terminals are marked with a plus sign (+), or a minus sign (-), and a letter, like "A".  Sometimes they have labels like "Send" or "Return", but you don’t really need to worry about that.  

Next, attach the ground cable to the metal plate on the battery, with the "A" side of the cable hooked up to the negative terminal.  

Then attach the other end of the ground cable to a ground connection on the car.  This could be a part under the hood, a little clip or terminal, or the metal part of the car under your car seat.  

Next attach the positive battery cable to the positive terminal on the battery.  

Then attach the other end of the positive cable to the positive terminal on the engine block, which is also called the battery terminal, and marked with a "+" sign.  

You may need to check with the other person to find where this is on their car.

You’re done!  Try turning on the engine to start the car now.

instruction: I like to host guests at my home from time to time, and I am gathering  recipes of different dishes and drinks to keep things interesting. I am interested in trying some Belgium dishes. Can you give me a recipe for Crevette grise?
chosen:
Sure, here’s a recipe from foodnetwork.com:

Recipe Type: Appetizer
Servings: 4
Prep time: 10 min
Cook time: 20 min

Crevettes grises (Gray shrimp) is a traditional Belgian appetizer. It’s a simple dish, but has a rich taste and very fresh shrimp.  
Ingredients:  
8 oz small shrimp (preferably from the north of the country, where they are smallest), shelled  
1.5 oz clarified butter  
1.5 oz flour  
2 cloves garlic, mashed with 1/2 oz breadcrumbs  
1 oz ham, shredded  
1/4 cup dry white wine  
1 1/2 oz low fat natural yogurt  
2 sprigs parsley, finely chopped  
2 oz water  
2 oz breadcrumbs  
2 oz butter, melted  
2 oz flour  
4 eggs, beaten

Method:  
Wash the shrimp and remove the heads, shells and tails.  
Rinse them, and dry.  
Mix the shrimp in a bowl with the ham, and the mashed garlic with breadcrumbs.  
Add the white wine.  
Let it marinade for 5 minutes.  
Heat up the clarified butter and put the flour in it.  
Keep stirring constantly, until the flour is absorbed and you get a paste.  
Put the marinated shrimp into the paste, and stir very well.  
In a skillet, add the yogurt and parsley and the water.  
Bring it to a boil and remove from the stove.  
Put the shrimp mixture on a plate.  
Take a spoon and make holes in it, filling each hole with the shrimp mixture.  
Put a small amount of water in a shallow bowl.  
Dip the shrimp into the water and then in the beaten egg.  
Put the shrimp on a lightly oiled baking sheet, and put the breadcrumbs and melted butter on top.  
Cook in a 350-degree oven for 20 minutes.  
The ideal way to serve it is to make shrimp balls with a teaspoon.  
These Crevettes grises are really good served with a cream sauce.

instruction: What's the origin for the succubus myth?
chosen: The story of the succubus came from classical mythology. The original succubi were evil spirits that appeared in dreams and seduced men. The succubus was often described as an attractive woman who would appear in a man's dreams and have sex with him. Eventually the idea of the succubus evolved into a female demon or incubus who preyed on men, often by having sex with them while they slept. Many cultures around the world have stories about these evil demons, and scholars believe the idea originated with ancient Mesopotamian religions. The succubus story is still widely believed in some cultures today, and has figured in works of popular fiction like the fictional TV show Supernatural.

The succubus myth originated many centuries ago in medieval Europe as an explanation for the phenomenon of "nightmares", or strange and frightening dreams experienced by humans.  The succubus, or demon lover, was imagined to be a seductive female demon who would tempt and seduce sleeping men in their dreams.  It was believed that through this physical interaction, the succubus would consume vital energy or life force from the male victim, causing weakness and fatigue upon waking.  The succubus was also believed to be a tangible reality in many cases, with reports of physical signs such as bite marks and sexually transmitted diseases attributed to visitations by the demon.  The succubus myth should be contrasted with the incubus myth, which similarly describes nighttime visitations by a demonic male entity which employs sexual activity in order to drain energy from sleeping females.  The two myths have many common features, but are distinguished by the gender of the demon performing the nocturnal seduction.

instruction: What is hydrogen peroxide used for?

It is used in a range of applications including the cleaning and disinfecting of wounds, as a bleach and disinfectant in labs and hospitals; to control fungus growth in agricultural and food applications, as a oven-cleaning product, as a rocket propellant; in the industrial detoxification of organic mordants; in fire extinguishers and fire suppression systems; and in rocket fuel. In personal care products, hydrogen peroxide is a commonly-used disinfectant in antiseptic ointments, creams, and soaps, and is also widely used as a hair bleaching product.

It is also used to disinfect drinking water and for preparing food, in the treatment of pool water, and in dentistry for whitening teeth. Hydrogen peroxide is also used in rocket propulsion and as a propellent for heat-seeking missiles. In industrial applications, it is used to bleach paper pulp and for foam manufacturing, to produce hydrogen used in refining metals, and to clean industrial equipment and produce other chemicals. The use of hydrogen peroxide in medicine, safety and handling considerations, and environmental impact are among the major topics of ongoing debate and study.

instruction: Can you tell me the proof that the big bang happened?

The big bang theory predicts that, because space is expanding, everything in the universe should be moving away from everything else.  This means that as far as we can see, everything should be getting further and further away from each other, which is what we’ve observed.

This, combined with an analysis of the cosmic microwave background radiation, suggests that about 400,000 years after the big bang, the universe was a hot dense soup.  A fraction of a second later, particles of matter cooled off enough to start clumping together.  The universe has been expanding and cooling ever since.

2 teaspoons dried parsley

Many of the first things I see when people ask a question like this are obvious, but I think that often people ignore the most basic parts of a healthy lifestyle.  Here’s my basic approach:

1. Make sure that you are getting enough exercise each day.  An adult should exercise at least 30 minutes per day, so try to be sure you are meeting that threshold.

2. Eat a variety of healthy foods throughout the day.  In particular, try to keep balanced meals that don’t have too many sweets or empty calories.

3. Try to keep yourself in good mental health.  If you are able to have a more positive outlook on life, you will be better able to maintain a healthy lifestyle, which in turn will contribute to your weight loss.

4. Try to avoid excessive and impulsive eating.  Cutting back on your portions and food choices can be helpful, but also keep in mind that our bodies need a certain number of calories each day, so you should also be sure that you are eating a lot of food.

5. Lastly, it is important that you exercise regularly and do not engage in unhealthy habits that lead to weight gain, such as heavy drinking or smoking
rejected: Absolutely! Would you like to hear about some diet and exercise strategies for healthy weight loss?

instruction: What is the difference between a Hurricane and a Tornado?
chosen:
Hurricanes typically start in the tropics and progress westwards, while tornadoes can originate from either the tropics or the mid-latitudes.  In both cases they can occur any time of year, but are more common in certain seasons.

Hurricanes are bigger storms, and have huge bands of rain and high winds, which often result in significant damage.  A hurricane can also spawn tornadoes, or a tornado can form inside a hurricane.  Tornadoes also come in two main varieties: large and small.  Large tornadoes can cause massive destruction and are often seen on the news, while smaller tornadoes are also common but often go unreported.
rejected: Hurricanes and tornados are both severe, large-scale weather events.  But there are some differences in their formation and behavior.  Hurricanes are huge swirling systems, thousands of miles across, that form over warm oceans.  They are fueded by heat and moisture from the ocean below, and they can cause devastating damage when they make landfall.  They can also cause huge storms and dangerous waves even before they make landfall.  Tornados are smaller and more localized, often forming from thunderstorms, and can cause major damage in their immediate area.  They also often move rapidly, with winds over 100 mph.

instruction: What causes erectile dysfunction?
chosen: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is the inability to achieve or maintain a penile erection adequate for sexual intercourse. This condition is usually due to physical problems or diseases, such as heart disease, stroke, diabetes, neurological conditions, and hormonal abnormalities. There are many different types of ED, some of which are associated with psychological causes, such as anxiety or stress. Treatments for ED include lifestyle changes, hormone therapy, medications, and penile implants. To discuss ED with a professional, please see a doctor or urologist. Erectile dysfunction is a serious medical condition and before treating it, be sure to consult with a physician.

instruction: What are some fundamental problems for interplanetary travel?
chosen: The first, and probably the most significant, challenge is the very high cost of simply reaching Mars, which is about 42 million miles away.  We could launch spacecrafts from the Earth’s surface to Mars, of course, but Mars travels at about 139 million miles per year, so such a trip would take a long time.  To move at this distance and speed more quickly, spacecrafts usually need to be launched from somewhere else outside Earth’s orbit, because otherwise they’d need to travel very fast in order to be able to catch up to the moving planet, and this limits the mass of the spacecraft.  Further, such a trip to Mars would take about 6 months, which is beyond the safe working lifetime of most spacecrafts.  Finally, it’s incredibly expensive to carry supplies to space (food, fuel, etc).  It’s estimated that these factors add up to make such an interplanetary trip unfeasibly expensive, so we’d need extremely advanced technologies to make it possible.
rejected: The major problems for interplanetary travel include the difficulties of spaceflight, and the hostile environments and radiation conditions in space and on other planets. In practice, interplanetary travel between the planets is a challenge requiring significant level of technological and logistical support. While spaceflight-related technologies such as rockets, spacecraft, and launch systems continue to advance, the Abraham Maslow problem - defined as the need for increasingly sophisticated and complex systems to sustain activities in harsh and alien environments - remains one of the larger impediments to developing long-term interplanetary expeditions. In addition, the relatively low level of solar energy on other planets, and the lack of atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen on the Moon and Mars, make the existing relatively short-term expeditions into space or to low earth orbit seem minor, and far too brief, in comparison to realistic long-term human habitation and missions in the solar system.  Other potential problems and obstacles for travel to other planets include extreme variances in temperature, pressure, radiation exposure, and gravitational forces, as well as the practical difficulties of limited energy and resources, logistical support issues, engineering challenges, and the tens to hundreds of millions of miles (and the corresponding time delays) required for travel and communication.

instruction: I've heard a lot about RSS feeds but I have no idea what they are. Can you explain them to me?

You can think of it as a standardized way for websites to send each other updates, much like how your email inbox works, except that the content is in a format that you're more likely to want to read (like web pages).
rejected: Sure, RSS stands for "Rich Site Summary", and it's a way to get news from the web onto your personal computer in a manageable format.  Let me give you an example.  Say I write an article about penguins, and I want to be able to keep track of how many people read that article.  So the penguin article comes with an RSS feed, which is a code that tells my computer to regularly check my article's URL (that's a unique internet address for the article) and report back on what it finds.  In other words, my article's RSS feed tells my computer to give me updates when someone reads my article.

Volvo recently made public that its new vehicle technology will only be enabled when the driver is ready and attentive, reducing the total number of crashes significantly. Most major auto makers have also announced plans to release fully self driving vehicles by 2021 and 2025.  Self driving car technology will certainly improve over time, but it will likely be many years before it is completely safe and reliable for use in all drivers and traffic conditions. instruction: Can stress affect the immune system?
chosen: Yes. Most notably, stress causes the body to release the hormones adrenaline and cortisol.  These chemicals increase heart rate and blood pressure, which are temporary responses to perceived danger.  They help the body to “fight” or “flee” a threat, and can activate changes in our metabolism, such as increasing sugar and fat reserves.  These physical changes are called the “fight-or-flight response”, and can be an evolutionary response that is part of our survival instincts.  Over time, these responses can become problematic.  Since the fight-or-flight response is a “physiological primitive” which our brains have not evolved to override, it’s possible that in a modern society, stressful situations can continue to trigger these responses.  When this happens, it’s a “psychosomatic response”.  Furthermore, there is some evidence that extreme stress or mental-health related issues can have an effect on the immune system.
rejected: Yes, definitely.  There is substantial evidence to suggest that emotional stress increases the risk of colds, stomach problems, as well as more severe things like heart disease and cancer.  But it is worth keeping in mind that the effects of stress are often not linear, but instead exhibit a J-curve pattern.  If your immune system is strong, stress may cause you to catch a few more colds, but ultimately your immune system should be much better off in the long term.

instruction: What is a logical fallacy?
chosen:
That’s a tricky question. A common definition of a logical fallacy is an argument that can be proved logically invalid. But in practice, that just seems to be a catch-all for any kind of faulty reasoning. I personally find it more helpful to classify fallacies by the kinds of reasoning that they make invalid. 
For example, there’s “equivocation” (also known as “amphiboly”), where words have a meaning that shifts over time. So I might say “If I went to the store, I’d buy a cake,” where I’m equivocating on the meaning of “I”. In this example, the original “I” refers to me, but later the “I” refers to you. The problem is that my statement doesn’t apply to you at all. This kind of fallacy is very common in everyday speech, so maybe it’s not a good example, but it’s one that comes to mind.
rejected: Do you mean in everyday language, or what?  The word “fallacy” comes from the Greek word “to fall”.  A “fallacy” is a mistake or misstep in reasoning.  And a “logical fallacy” is a mistake or misstep in reasoning that might arise from logical flaws.  You can think of logic as a method for reasoning that’s informed by strict rules for reasoning.  There are lots of different ways a fallacy can come about, but usually the rules of logic are not followed exactly, which means some inferences could have been false.  For example, one very common fallacy is that of “equivocation”: to equivocate is to take different meanings of a word at different times, which then causes you to draw an incorrect conclusion.

instruction: Can you help me to understand why Pluto was removed from the "planet" classification?
chosen: Pluto was a planet for almost 90 years, before 2006, when a scientific consensus was reached to change its classification. This was a difficult decision because the issue was still debated, and the impact of removing it from the “planetary” classification had serious implications. Before 2006, Pluto could be called a planet because, among other things, its orbit had the right shape for it to be classified that way, and because there was no evidence that it had a different origin from the other planets. In 2006, astronomers came to an agreement to remove Pluto from the planet class. The reasoning was that it was about a third the mass of the other planets and had a much different orbit. As such, it was less like the other planets than some of the other dwarf planets, which had the same orbit as Pluto’s.
rejected: The international astronomical community considered many different sources of evidence and came to the conclusion that Pluto does not satisfy the qualifications to be called a planet.  According to the official definition, a planet is a celestial body that is in orbit around a star, and the fact that Pluto does not have an independent orbit is a primary reason it was removed from the planet classification.

instruction: How difficult is it to grow flax?
chosen: Growing flax is actually not very difficult! It can grow in any soil that’s relatively moist, as well as in containers, in a greenhouse, or on a balcony. The seeds need warm soil and moisture to germinate, and once they take root they grow well with reasonable care. The most difficult part of growing flax is actually harvesting it, because the stems grow tall and need to be cut. The flax heads themselves are on top of the stems, and need to be harvested individually. Harvesting can be a bit difficult, and you need to be careful not to damage the heads of flax as you cut them. The heads are actually still alive, and they need to be harvested carefully so that you don’t damage them. If you want to grow flax for the seeds, you’ll want to collect the seed heads and let them dry completely, then you’ll want to separate the seeds from the chaff. You can do this by rubbing the heads between your fingers, or you can winnow them to separate the seeds.
rejected: Growing flax isn’t difficult, but it is labor-intensive.  First you need to prepare the soil where you want to grow it.  Make sure the soil is rich, and well-drained.  Then you’ll need to sow the seeds.  You’ll want to sow them very thinly, in rows about 18 inches apart.  The rows need to be straight, to make it easier to harvest the flax.  Once the seeds are sown, you’ll want to keep the soil moist, and make sure there are no weeds around the base of the plants.  Once the seedlings come up, you’ll need to thin them so they’re about 2 inches apart.  You’ll want to do this carefully, to ensure the plants grow straight, and remain healthy.  You’ll want to do this once they’re about 2 inches tall, and then again about once a month after that, until they’re mature, and you want them to grow to be about 6 inches tall.  Once they’re 6 inches tall, you’ll need to start picking the leaves, and also the stems.  It can take a couple of years for a flax patch to mature.

instruction: What can you tell me about Marie Curie's contributions to science?
chosen:
Marie Curie is most famous for being one of the discoverers of radium and polonium, as well as for having won a Nobel Prize in Physics. She also worked with her husband, Pierre, and they were both awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1903, with Marie winning the Nobel in 1911 for “her special merits of discovery in the field of radioactivity.” 

Marie also did extensive work on applications of X-rays. She is credited with making over 10,000 radiographs, along with inventing the first radiography equipment and creating a system of treatment and clinical testing based on the use of X-rays. 

Marie Curie also influenced non-science-related fields. She worked on behalf of child laborers, and worked to push for their rights. She founded the group “La Union féministe socialiste,” along with her friend, feminist Pauline Kergomard. Curie helped lead the fight for women's suffrage in Poland and in France, helping to win voting rights for French women in 1944.
